On this page you will find an ideal student paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end.

An Ideal Student Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

An ideal student is a student who treats education as a responsibility, not only as a race for marks. He attends classes regularly, listens to his teachers carefully, and asks questions when he does not understand a lesson. He studies every day, reviews his lessons before they are forgotten, and tries to understand ideas instead of memorising them without meaning.

An ideal student is also good in character. He respects his parents, teachers, and classmates, and follows the rules of his school. He is truthful, punctual, and helpful, and he admits his mistakes honestly. He keeps his body healthy through exercise, sleep, and play, because a healthy body helps concentration.

He does not become proud after success or hopeless after failure. He helps weaker classmates, keeps his notes organised, and uses his time well. In this way, he prepares himself not only for examinations but also for a useful life.

An Ideal Student Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

An ideal student is a student who treats education as a responsibility rather than a race for marks. Such a learner attends classes regularly, listens carefully, asks questions, and reviews lessons before they are forgotten. Instead of memorising every sentence, the student tries to understand ideas and explain them independently. He keeps a daily routine for study, revision, and rest, and he completes his homework and classwork on time. He prepares his lessons before class so that he can follow the teacher easily and take part in discussion.

Good study is balanced with good character. An ideal student respects parents, teachers, classmates, and school rules. The student is truthful, punctual, helpful, and willing to admit mistakes. He never copies in examinations and never looks down on weaker students. He avoids gossip and useless activities in his free time. Instead, he helps his classmates, shares his notes, and learns from group study. Exercise, sleep, and recreation are also important because a healthy body supports concentration and a fresh mind learns faster.

An excellent learner does not become proud after success or discouraged after failure. He finds out why he failed, corrects his weakness, and tries again with more care. He uses technology responsibly, for learning and research, not for wasting time. He also takes part in social service and school activities when he gets time. These habits prepare a person not only for examinations but also for useful citizenship. True excellence combines knowledge, discipline, kindness, and the courage to keep improving.

An Ideal Student Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

An ideal student is one who treats education as a responsibility rather than a race for marks. He understands that student life is the best time to build knowledge, character, and good habits for the future. So he attends classes regularly, listens to his teachers with attention, and asks questions whenever he does not understand a lesson. He studies every day according to a routine, reviews his lessons before they are forgotten, and completes his homework on time. Instead of memorising every sentence without meaning, he tries to understand ideas deeply and explain them in his own words. He keeps his notes organised and reads reference books.

But good marks alone do not make an ideal student. Character matters just as much as study. An ideal student respects his parents, teachers, and classmates, and he follows the rules of his school and society. He is truthful, punctual, honest, and helpful. He admits his mistakes, keeps his promises, and never cheats in examinations. He is kind to weaker classmates and learns from others without pride. He keeps his body healthy through regular exercise, enough sleep, and outdoor games, because a healthy body supports a fresh and attentive mind.

An ideal student also knows how to face both success and failure. Success does not make him proud, and failure does not make him hopeless. When he fails, he finds the reason, corrects his weakness, and works harder the next time. He uses mobile phones and the internet responsibly, mainly for learning, and avoids wasting hours on useless entertainment. He joins social service and school activities, which teach leadership and responsibility. In this way, an ideal student prepares himself not only for examinations but also for a useful and honourable life. True excellence is the combination of knowledge, discipline, kindness, and the courage to keep improving every day.

Bangla Meaning of An Ideal Student Paragraph

আদর্শ ছাত্রের বাংলা অর্থ

একজন আদর্শ ছাত্র শিক্ষাকে শুধু নম্বরের প্রতিযোগিতা মনে করে না, বরং দায়িত্ব মনে করে। সে নিয়মিত ক্লাসে যায়, শিক্ষকের কথা মনোযোগ দিয়ে শোনে এবং না বুঝলে প্রশ্ন করে। সে প্রতিদিন পড়াশোনা করে, পাঠ ভুলে যাওয়ার আগেই ঝালিয়ে নেয় এবং না বুঝে মুখস্থ করার বদলে বিষয়টি বুঝতে চেষ্টা করে।

একজন আদর্শ ছাত্র চরিত্রেও ভালো হয়। সে বাবা-মা, শিক্ষক ও সহপাঠীদের সম্মান করে এবং স্কুলের নিয়ম মেনে চলে। সে সত্যবাদী, সময়নিষ্ঠ ও পরোপকারী হয় এবং নিজের ভুল স্বীকার করতে দ্বিধা করে না। ব্যায়াম, ঘুম ও খেলাধুলার মাধ্যমে সে শরীর সুস্থ রাখে, কারণ সুস্থ শরীর পড়ায় মনোযোগ বাড়ায়।

সাফল্যে সে অহংকারী হয় না, আবার ব্যর্থতায় হতাশও হয় না। সে দুর্বল সহপাঠীদের সাহায্য করে, নোট গুছিয়ে রাখে এবং সময়ের সঠিক ব্যবহার করে। এভাবেই একজন আদর্শ ছাত্র শুধু পরীক্ষার জন্য নয়, একটি সুন্দর ও উপকারী জীবনের জন্য নিজেকে তৈরি করে।

Important Word Meanings

English WordBangla Meaning

Punctualসময়নিষ্ঠ
Truthfulসত্যবাদী

Exam Tips

  • Choose the version that matches your class: 150 words for Class 6–7, 250 words for Class 8–10 and SSC, 300 words for SSC and HSC.
  • Do not memorise the whole paragraph word by word. Learn the main points — regularity, understanding, character, health, and facing failure — and write them in your own sentences.
  • Keep one paragraph in one block. Do not break it into many small paragraphs unless the question asks for it.
  • Use the Bangla meaning to understand difficult words before you memorise the English version.
  • Revise the paragraph once the night before the exam instead of reading it for the first time in the hall.

On this page you will find a tree plantation paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end.

Tree Plantation Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

Tree plantation means planting trees in suitable places and looking after them until they grow. Trees give us oxygen, shade, fruit and timber. They also keep the soil firm with their roots, cool the air with their leaves, and give birds and animals a home. Trees keep our air clean and our weather balanced.

We can plant trees beside roads, around schools and ponds, and on unused land. Fruit trees give food and income, while big shade trees give comfort. We should choose healthy saplings, prepare the soil well, water them regularly and protect them from goats. Planting a tree is easy, but caring for it is the real work.

We must stop needless cutting and plant new trees in their place. Schools can hold a tree plantation programme, but the saplings need care all year, not only on that day. If every family plants a few trees, our country will be greener and healthier.

Tree Plantation Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

Tree plantation means planting trees in suitable places and caring for them until they grow into strong, useful trees. It is very important for Bangladesh because trees give us oxygen, shade, fruit, timber, fuel and medicine. Their roots hold the soil firm and stop it from washing away in rain and floods. Their leaves cool the air and give shelter to birds and other animals. Without enough trees, the air becomes hot and dry.

We can plant trees in many places: beside roads, around schools, colleges and ponds, in home gardens and on unused land. Fruit trees like mango, jackfruit and guava give food and extra income to a family. Big shade trees give comfort to travellers and workers in hot weather. Timber trees give wood for houses and furniture. Before planting, we should choose healthy saplings, prepare the soil well, and plant them at the right time, usually in the rainy season when water is easy to get.

Planting is only the first step. A young tree needs water, fencing and protection from goats and cattle. Many trees die because nobody looks after them after the planting day. So schools, clubs and local people should take responsibility for the trees they plant and check them regularly. We must also stop cutting trees without need and plant new ones in place of the trees we cut. If every family plants and protects a few trees, our villages and towns will become greener, cooler, cleaner and healthier for everyone.

Tree Plantation Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

Tree plantation means planting trees in suitable places and looking after them until they grow into strong and useful trees. It is one of the most important duties of the people of Bangladesh. Trees give us oxygen, shade, fruit, timber, fuel and medicine. Their roots hold the soil together and protect it from erosion. Their leaves take in carbon dioxide, give out oxygen and cool the air around them. Birds, bees and many other animals live on trees, so trees also protect the natural balance of our country.

There are many suitable places for planting trees. We can plant them beside roads, around schools and ponds, in home gardens, on river banks and on unused land. Fruit trees such as mango, jackfruit, litchi and guava give food and income to families. Timber trees such as teak, mahogany and rain tree give valuable wood. Medicinal plants like neem and tulsi are also useful. Before planting, we should select healthy saplings, prepare the soil well, and plant them at the proper time. The rainy season is the best time because young trees get water easily and grow fast.

However, planting a tree is not enough. A sapling needs regular water, protection from goats and cattle, and care for several years. Many trees die because people forget them after the planting ceremony. The government has also set a target of planting 25 crore trees in five years, which shows how seriously the country now takes this work. But no programme can succeed if saplings are left uncared for. Every school, office and family should take responsibility for the trees it plants. We must stop cutting trees without need, and plant two more whenever one is cut. If we all do this, Bangladesh will be greener and healthier, and future generations will thank us.

Bangla Meaning of Tree Plantation Paragraph

বৃক্ষরোপণের বাংলা অর্থ

বৃক্ষরোপণ মানে উপযুক্ত জায়গায় গাছ লাগানো এবং বড় না হওয়া পর্যন্ত তার যত্ন নেওয়া। গাছ আমাদের অক্সিজেন, ছায়া, ফল, কাঠ ও ওষুধ দেয়। গাছের শিকড় মাটি ধরে রাখে, পাতা বাতাস ঠান্ডা করে এবং পাখি ও অন্যান্য প্রাণীর আশ্রয় হয়। রাস্তার পাশে, স্কুলের চারপাশে, পুকুরের ধারে, বাড়ির বাগানে ও পতিত জমিতে গাছ লাগানো যায়। ফলের গাছ খাবার ও আয় দেয়, আর বড় ছায়াদার গাছ গরমে আরাম দেয়। সুস্থ চারা বেছে নিয়ে মাটি তৈরি করে নিয়মিত পানি দিতে হয় এবং ছাগল-গরু থেকে রক্ষা করতে হয়। গাছ লাগানো সহজ, কিন্তু তার যত্ন নেওয়াই আসল কাজ। অপ্রয়োজনে গাছ কাটা বন্ধ করে কাটা গাছের বদলে নতুন গাছ লাগাতে হবে। প্রতিটি পরিবার কয়েকটি গাছ লাগিয়ে যত্ন নিলে আমাদের দেশ আরও সবুজ, ঠান্ডা ও স্বাস্থ্যকর হবে।

On this page you will find a school magazine paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end.

A School Magazine Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

A school magazine is a collection of writing and artwork prepared by the students and teachers of a school. It is usually published once a year. It contains poems, essays, short stories, reports, drawings, puzzles, interviews and news of important school events. It shows the talent and creativity of the students.

A teacher guides the magazine, and a committee of students collects writings, edits them, arranges pictures and checks the proofs. This work teaches planning, teamwork and careful reading. A shy student may gain confidence when a poem or story of his own appears in print.

A school magazine also keeps a record of school life. Readers learn about prizes, clubs, sports, festivals and the achievements of the year. It should welcome writings from all students, not only from the best ones. In this way it becomes both a memory of the school and a training ground for young writers.

A School Magazine Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

A school magazine is a collection of writing and artwork prepared by the students and teachers of a school. It is usually published once a year and contains poems, essays, short stories, reports, drawings, puzzles, interviews and news of important school events. It is not a textbook but a mirror of school life, showing the talent, ideas and creativity of the students. A good magazine gives every student a chance to see his or her own work in print.

Publishing a magazine is team work. A teacher usually acts as the editor and guides an editorial committee of students. The members collect writings from their classmates, select the best pieces, correct spelling and grammar, arrange illustrations and check the proofs before printing. This work teaches planning, cooperation, patience and respect for the ideas of others. It also teaches students to accept correction, because even a good piece of writing becomes better after careful editing. A shy student may discover new confidence when a poem or report of his own appears in the magazine.

A school magazine also preserves the memory of a school year. Future readers can learn about prize-giving ceremonies, sports days, cultural programmes, clubs and the achievements of students and teachers. It should welcome writings of different kinds and from students of different abilities, not only perfect pieces from the best students. With honest editing and encouragement from teachers, a school magazine becomes both a record of school life and a training ground for future writers, journalists and artists.

A School Magazine Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

A school magazine is a collection of writing and artwork prepared by the students and teachers of a school. It is usually published once a year. It contains poems, essays, short stories, reports, drawings, puzzles, interviews and news of important school events. It is not a textbook but a mirror of school life, showing the talent and creativity of the students. A good magazine gives every student a chance to see his or her own work in print.

Publishing a magazine is real team work. A teacher usually acts as the editor and guides an editorial committee formed from students of different classes. The members collect poems, essays and stories from their classmates, select the best pieces, correct spelling and grammar, arrange illustrations, and check the proofs carefully before printing. This long process teaches planning, cooperation, patience and respect for the ideas of others. Students also learn to accept correction, because even good writing becomes better after honest editing. A quiet student may discover new confidence when a poem of his own appears in print.

A school magazine also preserves the character of a school during a particular year. Years later, readers can learn about prize-giving ceremonies, sports days, cultural programmes, debating clubs, science fairs and the achievements of students and teachers. It is a record that no other school document keeps so fully. A magazine should welcome writings of different kinds and from students of different abilities, rather than publishing only perfect pieces from the best students. With encouragement from teachers and honest editing, it becomes both a precious memory of school life and a training ground for future writers, journalists, teachers and artists. Every school should therefore publish a magazine regularly and give its students a fair chance to contribute.

Bangla Meaning of A School Magazine Paragraph

স্কুল ম্যাগাজিনের বাংলা অর্থ

স্কুল ম্যাগাজিন হলো একটি স্কুলের ছাত্রছাত্রী ও শিক্ষকদের লেখা ও ছবির সংকলন। এটি সাধারণত বছরে একবার প্রকাশিত হয়। এতে কবিতা, প্রবন্ধ, ছোটগল্প, প্রতিবেদন, ছবি, ধাঁধা, সাক্ষাৎকার এবং স্কুলের গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অনুষ্ঠানের খবর থাকে। একজন শিক্ষক সম্পাদকের দায়িত্ব পালন করেন এবং ছাত্রদের একটি সম্পাদনা কমিটি লেখা সংগ্রহ, সম্পাদনা ও ছাপার কাজ করে। এই কাজ ছাত্রদের পরিকল্পনা, সহযোগিতা ও যত্নশীল পড়াশোনা শেখায়। লাজুক ছাত্রও নিজের লেখা ছাপা দেখে আত্মবিশ্বাস পায়। স্কুল ম্যাগাজিন একটি বছরের স্কুলজীবনের স্মৃতি ধরে রাখে। এতে সব ছাত্রের লেখার সুযোগ থাকা উচিত, শুধু সেরাদের নয়। এভাবেই ম্যাগাজিন স্কুলজীবনের স্মৃতি ও ভবিষ্যৎ লেখকদের প্রশিক্ষণের ক্ষেত্র হয়ে ওঠে। ভালো ম্যাগাজিন ছাত্রদের পড়া ও লেখার প্রতি আগ্রহ বাড়ায়।

On this page you will find a winter morning paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, and the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end.

A Winter Morning Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

A winter morning is a quiet, beautiful morning of the cold season. Before sunrise, everything is covered with thick fog. Trees, houses and roads look blurred in the fog. The air is cold and sharp, so people wrap themselves in warm clothes, shawls and blankets.

When the sun rises, golden light removes the fog. Dew drops shine on the grass like pearls, and birds begin to sing in the trees. Farmers go to the fields, and children hurry to school after warming themselves by the fire. Tea stalls become busy because a hot cup of tea gives comfort in the cold.

A winter morning is pleasant for those who can enjoy it. Date juice, pitha and warm sunshine are the joys of the season. But poor people suffer because they have no warm clothes or shelter. We should help them with food and blankets. A winter morning teaches us both beauty and kindness.

A Winter Morning Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

A winter morning is one of the most beautiful sights of the cold season in Bangladesh. It comes slowly, wrapped in thick fog. Before sunrise, trees, houses and roads look blurred, and the far end of the village road disappears in the mist. The air is cold and sharp, and people wrap themselves in sweaters, shawls and blankets. Nature seems asleep, and even the birds remain silent until the sun appears.

The scene changes when the sun rises. Golden light slowly melts the fog, dew drops shine on the grass like pearls, and birds begin to sing in the trees. Farmers lead their cattle to the fields, fishermen go to the rivers, and children hurry to school after warming their hands by a small fire. Tea stalls become busy places because a hot cup of tea gives workers comfort before the day begins. In the villages, people enjoy date juice, pitha and fresh vegetables, which are special foods of winter.

A winter morning is pleasant for those who can enjoy it at leisure, sitting in the warm sunshine. But it is hard for the poor. Many poor people have no warm clothes, no blanket and no proper shelter, so they shiver through the cold morning. Old people and children suffer the most. We should remember them and help them with blankets, warm clothes and food. A winter morning is thus a mixture of beauty and hardship. It delights our eyes, but it also teaches us sympathy and kindness towards those who suffer in the cold.

A Winter Morning Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

A winter morning is one of the most beautiful and memorable sights of the cold season in Bangladesh. It arrives slowly, wrapped in thick fog. Before sunrise, trees, rooftops and roads look blurred, and the far end of the village road disappears in the mist. The air is cold and sharp, so people wrap themselves in sweaters, shawls and blankets. Nature seems to sleep, and even the birds remain silent until the first light appears. Everything looks calm and quiet in the fog.

The scene changes when the sun rises. Golden light slowly melts the fog, dew drops shine on the grass like pearls, and birds begin to sing from the branches. Farmers lead their cattle to the fields, fishermen go to the rivers, and children hurry to school after warming their hands by a small fire. Tea stalls become busy, because a hot cup of tea comforts workers before the day begins. In the villages, people enjoy date juice, pitha and warm sunshine, the special joys of winter. A winter morning is fresh, bright and full of life once the fog is gone.

However, a winter morning is not pleasant for everyone. It is a season of suffering for the poor. Many poor people have no warm clothes, no blanket and no proper shelter, so they shiver through the cold morning. Old people and little children suffer the most, and many fall sick. Rich people enjoy the warm sunshine, but the poor cannot enjoy it at all. We should remember them and share our blankets, warm clothes and food with them. A winter morning is thus a mixture of beauty and hardship. It delights our eyes, but it also teaches us that comfort should not make us forget the suffering of others.

Bangla Meaning of A Winter Morning Paragraph

শীতের সকালের বাংলা অর্থ

শীতের সকাল শীতকালের একটি শান্ত ও সুন্দর সকাল। সূর্য ওঠার আগে সবকিছু ঘন কুয়াশায় ঢাকা থাকে। গাছপালা, ঘরবাড়ি ও রাস্তা ঝাপসা দেখায় এবং রাস্তার দূরের প্রান্ত দেখা যায় না। বাতাস ঠান্ডা ও তীক্ষ্ণ হয়, তাই মানুষ গরম কাপড়, শাল ও কম্বল জড়িয়ে নেয়। সূর্য উঠলে সোনালি আলো ধীরে ধীরে কুয়াশা সরিয়ে দেয়, ঘাসের ওপর শিশির মুক্তার মতো জ্বলজ্বল করে এবং পাখি গান গাইতে শুরু করে। কৃষক গরু নিয়ে মাঠে যায়, শিশুরা আগুনে হাত গরম করে স্কুলে ছোটে। খেজুরের রস, পিঠা, তাজা সবজি ও রোদ শীতের আনন্দ। কিন্তু গরিব মানুষের গরম কাপড় ও আশ্রয় নেই বলে তারা কষ্ট পায়। আমাদের কম্বল ও খাবার দিয়ে তাদের সাহায্য করা উচিত। শীতের সকাল আমাদের সৌন্দর্য ও দয়ার শিক্ষা দেয়।

Important Word Meanings

English WordBangla Meaning
Fogকুয়াশা
Dewশিশির
Mistকুয়াশা
Blanketকম্বল
Shiverকাঁপা
Pleasantআনন্দদায়ক
Hardshipকষ্ট
Sympathyসহানুভূতি
Leisureঅবসর
Mysteriousরহস্যময়

Exam Tips

  • Choose the version that matches your class: 150 words for Class 6–7, 250 words for Class 8–10 and SSC, 300 words for SSC and HSC.
  • Learn the main points — fog before sunrise, the change after sunrise, joys of winter, suffering of the poor — and write them in your own sentences.
  • Do not memorise the whole paragraph word by word; practise writing it once from memory.
  • Use the Bangla meaning to understand difficult words before you memorise the English version.
  • Keep the paragraph in one block and revise it once the night before the exam.

On this page you will find a load shedding paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end.

Load Shedding Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

Load shedding means stopping the supply of electricity in an area for some time. It happens when the demand for electricity is more than the supply. Sometimes it also happens because of a fault in a power plant, a broken line, or a storm. In Bangladesh, load shedding is a common problem, and it causes much suffering to people.

When the electricity goes off, our daily life comes to a stop. Students cannot study at night, fans and lights stop working, and people suffer in the heat. Food in the refrigerator may go bad, water pumps stop, and shops and factories cannot work. Hospitals also face great trouble because many machines need electricity.

To reduce load shedding, we should use electricity carefully and not waste it. The government should build more power plants and use solar power. If we all save electricity, our life will become easier.

Load Shedding Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

Load shedding means the planned stopping of electricity supply in an area for a certain time. It happens when the demand for electricity is greater than the supply. Sometimes it also happens because of a shortage of fuel, a fault in a power plant, damaged lines, or a storm. In Bangladesh, load shedding is a common problem. It disturbs our daily life and slows down the progress of the country.

When the power goes off, everything comes to a stop. Students cannot study at night, and it becomes very hard for them to prepare for examinations. Fans, lights, computers, and mobile phones stop working. People suffer greatly in the heat, and food kept in refrigerators may go bad. Water pumps stop, so people cannot get water easily. Shops, offices, and factories lose working hours, and production falls. During a long power cut, mobile networks may also fail, and students who depend on online classes lose their lessons. This wastes time and money for everyone. Hospitals face serious trouble because many patients depend on machines that run on electricity.

Load shedding can be reduced in many ways. The government should build more power plants, repair old lines, and stop illegal connections. Solar power and other renewable sources should be used more. We should also use electricity wisely. We should switch off lights and fans when we do not need them and use energy-saving bulbs. If the government and the people work together, load shedding can be reduced, and our life will become more comfortable.

Load Shedding Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

Load shedding means the planned interruption of electricity supply in an area for a certain period. It takes place when the demand for electricity is greater than the supply. It may also happen because of a shortage of fuel, a fault in a power plant, damaged transmission lines, or a natural disaster like a storm. In Bangladesh, load shedding is a familiar problem. It causes great suffering to people and hampers the development of the country.

Load shedding disturbs every part of our life. Students suffer most because they cannot study at night, especially before examinations. Without light, they cannot read, and without fans, they cannot sleep well in the heat. As a result, their studies are badly hampered. In homes, food kept in refrigerators may spoil, water pumps stop working, and people cannot use computers, televisions, or mobile phones. In hospitals, the problem is even more serious, because the lives of many patients depend on electrical machines. Doctors and nurses face great difficulty during an operation when the power goes off.

Our economy also suffers from load shedding. Factories cannot run their machines, so production falls and workers lose their jobs or working hours. Small shops and businesses lose customers, and farmers cannot run irrigation pumps in time. Repeated power cuts can also damage electrical appliances when the current returns suddenly.

To solve this problem, the government should build more power plants, repair the old power lines, and prevent illegal connections. More use should be made of solar power and other renewable sources of energy. People should also use electricity carefully, switch off unnecessary lights and fans, and use energy-saving appliances. If the authorities publish a regular schedule, people can plan their work. With proper planning and responsible use, load shedding can be reduced, and the country can move forward.

Bangla Meaning of Load Shedding Paragraph

লোডশেডিং অনুচ্ছেদের বাংলা অর্থ

লোডশেডিং মানে কোনো এলাকায় কিছু সময়ের জন্য বিদ্যুৎ সরবরাহ বন্ধ রাখা। বিদ্যুতের চাহিদা সরবরাহের চেয়ে বেশি হলে এটি ঘটে। কখনো কখনো বিদ্যুৎকেন্দ্রের ত্রুটি, লাইন নষ্ট হওয়া বা ঝড়ের কারণেও এটি হয়। বাংলাদেশে লোডশেডিং একটি সাধারণ সমস্যা এবং এটি মানুষের অনেক কষ্টের কারণ।

বিদ্যুৎ চলে গেলে আমাদের দৈনন্দিন জীবন থেমে যায়। শিক্ষার্থীরা রাতে পড়াশোনা করতে পারে না, পাখা ও বাতি বন্ধ হয়ে যায় এবং গরমে মানুষ কষ্ট পায়। ফ্রিজের খাবার নষ্ট হতে পারে, পানির পাম্প বন্ধ হয়ে যায় এবং দোকান ও কারখানা কাজ করতে পারে না। হাসপাতালেও বড় সমস্যা হয়, কারণ অনেক যন্ত্র বিদ্যুতে চলে।

লোডশেডিং কমাতে আমাদের বিদ্যুৎ সাবধানে ব্যবহার করা উচিত এবং অপচয় করা উচিত নয়। সরকারের উচিত আরও বিদ্যুৎকেন্দ্র তৈরি করা এবং সৌরশক্তি ব্যবহার করা। আমরা সবাই বিদ্যুৎ সাশ্রয় করলে আমাদের জীবন সহজ হবে।

  • Learn the structure first — meaning, causes, effects on students and hospitals, effects on the economy, and solutions — then write it in your own sentences.
  • Do not memorise the whole paragraph word by word. Remember the main points and connect them with simple linking words like firstly, secondly, and finally.
  • Use the Bangla meaning to understand difficult words before you memorise the English version.

item.title: How to Write an Application: Format, Examples & Tips
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Application writing is an important part of English writing in Bangladesh. Students may need to write an application to the headmaster, principal, department
item.content:encoded:
Application writing is an important part of English writing in Bangladesh. Students may need to write an application to the headmaster, principal, department head, or another authority for different reasons.

For example, you may need to write an application for leave, a testimonial, a transfer certificate, permission for a study tour, or another school or college matter. University students and job seekers also write formal applications for academic and professional purposes.

The good news is that most formal applications follow a simple structure. Once you understand the format, you can write an application for almost any situation.

This guide explains the basic application writing format and provides examples for school, college, university, and job applications.

What Is an Application?

An application is a formal written request made to a person or authority.

For example:

  • A student writes to the headmaster for leave.
  • A student writes to the principal for a testimonial.
  • A university student writes to the examination office for a transcript.
  • A student writes to an authority for permission to join a study tour.
  • A job seeker writes to an employer to apply for a position.

The purpose of an application should be clear from the beginning. Avoid unnecessary information and explain exactly what you are requesting.

Basic Application Writing Format

A formal application usually contains these parts:

  1. Date
  2. Name and designation of the recipient
  3. Institution or organisation
  4. Address
  5. Subject
  6. Salutation
  7. Main body
  8. Closing
  9. Name and identifying information of the applicant

A simple structure looks like this:

Date

The [Designation] [Institution Name] [Address]

Subject: Application for [purpose].

Sir/Madam,

First paragraph: Introduce yourself and explain why you are writing.

Second paragraph: Give the necessary details about your situation.

Final paragraph: Clearly state what you are requesting.

Yours faithfully/obediently, [Your Name] [Class/Department] [Roll/ID]

The exact format can vary between institutions, so students should follow any specific instructions given by their school, college, university, or employer.

1. Application for Leave

A leave application is written when you need permission to remain absent from school, college, or another institution.

Example: Leave Application for Illness

15 January 2026

The Headmaster Ideal High School Motijheel, Dhaka

Subject: Application for leave of absence.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am a student of Class IX, Section B, of your school. I have been suffering from a high fever for the last three days, and the doctor has advised me to take rest.

For this reason, I will not be able to attend school from 15 January to 18 January 2026. I therefore request you to kindly grant me leave for these four days.

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Md. Rakib Hasan Class IX, Section B Roll No. 17

What to include in a leave application

Make sure you mention:

  • The reason for your absence
  • The dates of your leave
  • Your class or department
  • Your roll or student ID
  • Any supporting document if the institution requires one

Do not write a long explanation. Give only the information the authority needs.

For a ready-made example, see our Application for Leave of Absence: Class 6 to 12 Students.

2. Application for a Testimonial

A testimonial is an official document that may provide information about a student's academic record, conduct, or period of study at an institution.

Students may need a testimonial after completing SSC or HSC or when applying for further education or other purposes.

Example: Testimonial Application

10 February 2026

The Principal Dhaka College New Market, Dhaka

Subject: Application for a testimonial.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I passed the HSC examination in 2025 from your college under the Dhaka Education Board. I am now preparing to apply for higher studies and require a testimonial from the college.

I therefore request you to kindly issue me a testimonial at your earliest convenience. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Sumaiya Akter HSC 2025, Science Group Roll No. 124356

Tip for students

If the institution has a specific testimonial form, use that form instead of writing a separate application. Some Bangladeshi institutions provide their own testimonial forms with fields for student information and academic details.

You can also read a full example in our Application for Testimonial For Class 6, 7, 8, SSC and HSC.

3. Application for an Academic Transcript

University students may need an academic transcript when applying for higher studies, scholarships, employment, or other official purposes.

The procedure is different from one university to another. Some universities require a specific form, fee payment, clearance, or supporting documents.

Example

22 March 2026

The Controller of Examinations University of Dhaka Dhaka-1000

Subject: Application for issuance of academic transcript.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I completed my Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science and Engineering from your university in 2025. I now require an official academic transcript for my application for higher studies abroad.

I have completed the required payment and attached the necessary documents with this application.

I therefore request you to kindly issue two copies of my official academic transcript.

Yours faithfully, Mohammad Tanvir Ahmed Registration No. 2021-715-001 Session: 2020–2021 Department of CSE

Important

Before submitting a university application, check your university's current instructions. Do not assume that every university uses the same process.

4. Application for a Transfer Certificate

A transfer certificate application is generally written when a student needs official permission or documentation to leave one institution and continue studies elsewhere.

Example

20 April 2026

The Principal ABC College Dhaka

Subject: Application for a transfer certificate.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am a student of Class XII of your college. My family is moving to another city, and I need to continue my studies there.

I therefore request you to kindly issue me a transfer certificate so that I can complete the necessary admission formalities at another institution.

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Rahim Ahmed Class XII Roll No. 25 Science Group

For another full example, see our Application for Transfer Certificate.

5. Application for Permission to Join a Study Tour

Students may need permission from their school or college authority before joining an educational tour or study tour.

Example

5 May 2026

The Headmaster ABC High School Dhaka

Subject: Application for permission to join a study tour.

Sir,

With due respect, we, the students of Class X, would like to arrange an educational study tour to the National Museum in Dhaka. Such a visit would give us an opportunity to learn more about the history and culture of Bangladesh outside the classroom.

We therefore request you to kindly grant us permission to arrange the study tour under the guidance of our teachers.

We shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, The students of Class X ABC High School Dhaka

Tip

For a group application, write on behalf of the students and clearly mention the proposed destination, purpose, and supervision arrangements when relevant.

6. Job Application Letter

A job application is different from a school application. Instead of asking a school authority for permission or a document, you are introducing yourself to an employer and explaining why you are suitable for a particular position.

A modern job application should be concise and specific.

Example

5 April 2026

The Head of Human Resources ABC Bank Limited Gulshan, Dhaka

Subject: Application for the position of Management Trainee Officer.

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to apply for the position of Management Trainee Officer advertised on your company's website.

I recently completed my BBA in Finance from North South University with a CGPA of 3.78. During my undergraduate studies, I completed a three-month internship with a commercial bank, where I gained practical experience in credit analysis and customer service.

I believe my academic background, internship experience, and communication skills would allow me to contribute effectively to your organisation. My CV and relevant academic documents are attached for your consideration.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my qualifications in an interview.

Yours faithfully, Nusrat Jahan nusrat.jahan@example.com +880 1XXX-XXXXXX

Job application tip

Do not copy the same application for every job.

Mention the actual position, organisation, and skills that are relevant to the job. Your application should support your CV rather than repeat everything in it.

7. Application for a Character Certificate

A character certificate or similar official document may be requested for admission, employment, or other purposes.

The exact name and procedure can vary by institution.

Example

12 June 2026

The Headmaster ABC High School Dhaka

Subject: Application for a character certificate.

Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I was a student of your school and passed the SSC examination in 2026. I now require a character certificate for my further studies.

I therefore request you to kindly issue me a character certificate mentioning my conduct and period of study at the institution.

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours obediently, Sadia Islam SSC 2026 Roll No. 123456

How to Write an Application Step by Step

If you have never written a formal application before, follow these steps.

Step 1: Identify the person you are writing to

Find out who should receive the application.

For example:

  • The Headmaster
  • The Principal
  • The Head of the Department
  • The Controller of Examinations
  • The Human Resources Manager

Use the correct designation.

Step 2: Write a clear subject

The subject should tell the reader what you want.

Good examples:

  • Application for leave of absence
  • Application for a testimonial
  • Application for issuance of an academic transcript
  • Application for a transfer certificate
  • Application for permission to join a study tour

Do not write a long subject.

Step 3: Introduce yourself

Tell the reader who you are.

For example:

I am a student of Class X, Section A, of your school.

A university student could write:

I am a student of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering.

Step 4: Explain the reason

Give the important facts related to your request.

For a leave application, mention the reason and dates.

For a testimonial, explain why you need it.

For a transcript, explain what you need and, if relevant, what the transcript is for.

Step 5: Make your request clearly

Do not make the reader guess what you want.

For example:

I therefore request you to kindly grant me leave for three days.

Step 6: End politely

Use an appropriate formal closing.

For example:

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Then add your name and relevant identification details.

Common Mistakes in Application Writing

Students often make simple mistakes that can make an application look careless.

1. Forgetting the subject

The subject helps the reader understand the purpose of the application quickly.

2. Writing too much

A formal application should contain the information necessary to understand and process the request. Avoid unrelated stories.

3. Using informal language

Avoid expressions such as:

  • Hi Sir
  • What's up
  • I wanna request
  • Please help me out
  • Thanks a lot

Use polite and formal language instead.

4. Using unnecessary difficult words

You do not need complicated English to write a good application.

For example:

I would like to request you to kindly grant me leave.

is clear and sufficient.

A simple sentence is usually better than a long sentence filled with difficult words.

5. Forgetting personal details

For school and college applications, include the details needed to identify you, such as:

  • Name
  • Class
  • Section
  • Roll number
  • Registration number
  • Department
  • Student ID

Only include information that is relevant to the application.

6. Using the wrong closing

Choose the closing according to the situation and the style required by your institution.

For traditional school applications, “Yours obediently” is commonly used. For professional applications, “Yours faithfully” or “Yours sincerely” may be more appropriate depending on how you address the recipient.

Yours Obediently, Yours Faithfully, or Yours Sincerely?

These expressions are often confusing for students.

Yours obediently

This is commonly found in traditional school and college applications addressed to teachers or institutional authorities.

Yours faithfully

This is commonly used in formal correspondence when you do not address the recipient by name, especially in British-style business writing.

Example:

Dear Sir/Madam, Yours faithfully,

Yours sincerely

This is commonly used when you address the recipient by name.

Example:

Dear Mr Karim, Yours sincerely,

However, institutions may have their own preferred format. If your school or university gives you a prescribed format, follow it.

Application Writing Format for SSC and HSC Students

For SSC and HSC students, application writing is also an important part of English writing practice.

Common topics include:

  • Application for leave
  • Application for a testimonial
  • Application for a transfer certificate
  • Application for a seat in the school hostel
  • Application for permission to arrange a study tour
  • Application for setting up a canteen
  • Application for improving library facilities
  • Application for arranging a cultural programme

For examination practice, first understand the format. Then practise writing different applications instead of memorising one answer word for word.

A memorised application may not fit a new question exactly.

Application Writing vs. Formal Letter Writing

These two types of writing are related, but they have different purposes.

An application is usually a formal request made to an authority.

A formal letter can have a wider purpose, such as making a complaint, requesting information, giving notice, or communicating with an organisation.

For example:

Application: Application to the principal for leave.

Formal letter: Letter to the editor about traffic congestion in Dhaka.

Knowing the purpose helps you choose the right format.

If you need to practise formal letter writing, read our Letter How to improve English for a complete example.

Quick Application Writing Template

You can use this template when you need to write a new application.

[Date]

The [Designation] [Institution Name] [Address]

Subject: Application for [purpose].

Sir/Madam,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am [your position/class/department].

[Explain the reason for your application and provide the important details.]

I therefore request you to kindly [clearly state what you want].

I shall be grateful for your kind consideration.

Yours faithfully/obediently, [Your Name] [Class/Department] [Roll/Student ID]

Use this as a framework, not as a paragraph to memorise. Change the details and sentences according to the situation.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the format of an application in Bangladesh?

A formal application generally includes the date, recipient's designation and institution, subject, salutation, body, closing, and the applicant's identifying details. The exact format may vary depending on the institution.

How do I start an application?

Start by identifying the recipient and writing a clear subject. In the first paragraph, introduce yourself and explain the reason for writing.

How long should a formal application be?

For most school and college applications, one or two short paragraphs are enough. Include the necessary information without adding unrelated details.

Should I write an application by hand?

Follow the instructions of the institution or organisation. Some schools may prefer handwritten applications, while universities and employers may require typed or online submissions.

What paper size should I use?

If the institution has not specified a paper size, A4 is a practical choice for a typed formal document. However, always follow the instructions provided by the receiving institution.

Can I use the same application format for every topic?

You can use the same basic structure, but the content should change according to your purpose. A leave application, testimonial application, university transcript request, and job application should not contain the same body text.

Should I memorise application examples for exams?

It is better to understand the format and practise different topics. Memorising complete applications can make it difficult to answer questions that use a different situation.

Final Tips for Writing a Good Application

Before submitting your application, check these points:

  • Is the recipient correct?
  • Is the subject clear?
  • Did you explain the reason?
  • Did you make your request clear?
  • Did you include your class, roll, ID, or department where necessary?
  • Did you use polite and formal language?
  • Did you check spelling and grammar?
  • Did you follow any instructions given by the institution?
  • Did you remove unnecessary information?

A good application does not need complicated English. It needs a clear purpose, correct information, polite language, and a suitable format.

Once you understand the basic structure, you can write applications for school, college, university, and professional situations with much more confidence.

Air Pollution Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

Air pollution means the air becomes dirty and unsafe to breathe. It happens when smoke, dust, poisonous gases and tiny harmful particles mix with the air. Smoke from vehicles, factories and brick kilns, dust from construction work, and the burning of rubbish are the main causes of air pollution in our country.

Polluted air is very harmful to our health. It irritates our eyes and throat, and it can cause asthma, cough and heart disease. Children, old people and those who work outdoors suffer the most. Air pollution also damages crops, buildings and animals, and it makes the climate warmer.

We must work together to keep the air clean. The government should enforce laws, control smoke from factories and vehicles, and improve public transport. We should not burn rubbish, and we should plant more trees and use clean energy. Clean air is necessary for a healthy life.

Air Pollution Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

Air pollution means the air around us becomes dirty and unsafe to breathe. It happens when smoke, dust, poisonous gases and tiny harmful particles mix with the air in large amounts. In Bangladesh, the main causes are smoke from motor vehicles, factories and brick kilns, dust from construction work and broken roads, and the burning of rubbish and dry leaves. In crowded cities, the problem becomes worse when the wind is weak and the smoke cannot blow away.

Polluted air is very harmful to our health. It irritates our eyes, nose and throat, and it can cause cough, asthma, lung disease and heart disease. Children, old people and people who work outdoors, such as rickshaw-pullers and construction workers, suffer the most. Air pollution also harms crops, animals and buildings. It makes the climate warmer by increasing harmful gases in the atmosphere. When the air is very polluted, even healthy people feel tired and uncomfortable.

We must all work together to keep the air clean. The government should enforce laws against smoke, improve public transport so that fewer private cars are needed, control dust at construction sites and encourage clean energy like solar power. We as citizens should not burn rubbish, should keep our vehicles in good condition, and should plant trees, which clean the air naturally. Schools can teach children about the dangers of polluted air. Clean air is not a luxury; it is necessary for the health and life of everyone.

Air Pollution Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

Air pollution means the air around us becomes dirty and unsafe to breathe. It occurs when smoke, dust, poisonous gases and tiny harmful particles enter the atmosphere in harmful amounts. In Bangladesh, the main sources are exhaust from motor vehicles, smoke from factories and brick kilns, dust from construction work and broken roads, and the burning of rubbish, dry leaves and crop waste. In crowded cities, the problem becomes serious in the dry winter months, when little rain washes the dust away. Air pollution is now a great threat to public health in our country.

Breathing polluted air is very harmful to the human body. It irritates the eyes, nose and throat, and it can cause cough, asthma, bronchitis, lung disease and heart disease. Children, old people and outdoor workers suffer the most, because they breathe polluted air for many hours every day. Air pollution also damages crops, weakens animals, blackens buildings and harms the climate by adding greenhouse gases to the atmosphere. On very polluted days, even healthy people feel tired. Treating pollution-related diseases is also a heavy burden on poor families.

Preventing air pollution needs both government action and personal responsibility. The authorities should enforce emission rules strictly, improve bus and train services so fewer private cars are needed, control dust at construction sites, and promote clean energy such as solar power. Citizens should also play their part: we should not burn rubbish or leaves, we should keep vehicles in good condition, we should walk or use public transport for short journeys, and we should plant trees, which clean the air naturally. Schools and the media can teach people about the dangers of polluted air. Clean air is the right of every citizen, and protecting it is a shared duty, because everyone depends on the air we breathe.

বায়ু দূষণ মানে আমাদের চারপাশের বাতাস নোংরা ও শ্বাস নেওয়ার অনুপযুক্ত হয়ে যাওয়া। যানবাহন, কারখানা ও ইটভাটার ধোঁয়া, নির্মাণকাজের ধুলো এবং আবর্জনা পোড়ানোর ধোঁয়া বাতাসে মিশে বায়ু দূষণ ঘটায়। দূষিত বাতাস চোখ ও গলা জ্বালা করে এবং হাঁপানি, কাশি, ফুসফুস ও হৃদরোগের কারণ হতে পারে। শিশু, বৃদ্ধ ও বাইরে কাজ করা মানুষ সবচেয়ে বেশি ক্ষতিগ্রস্ত হয়। বায়ু দূষণ ফসল, পশুপাখি ও ভবনেরও ক্ষতি করে এবং জলবায়ু উষ্ণ করে। বাতাস পরিষ্কার রাখতে সরকারকে আইন প্রয়োগ করতে হবে, গণপরিবহন উন্নত করতে হবে এবং পরিচ্ছন্ন জ্বালানি ব্যবহারে উৎসাহ দিতে হবে। আমাদের আবর্জনা পোড়ানো বন্ধ করে বেশি করে গাছ লাগাতে হবে। পরিচ্ছন্ন বাতাস সুস্থ জীবনের জন্য অপরিহার্য।

My Hobby Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

My favourite hobby is gardening. I grow flowers, herbs, and a few vegetables in pots and in a small patch beside our home. I loosen the soil, sow seeds, water the plants, and remove weeds. Watching a seed become a living plant teaches me patience and care.

Gardening refreshes me after study and gives me gentle exercise. Green plants make the surroundings cooler and more attractive, while herbs and vegetables can provide fresh food. I reuse kitchen containers as planters and avoid wasting water. Sometimes I share seedlings with my neighbours. This hobby has made me more interested in nature and more aware that healthy surroundings depend on daily responsibility. I also keep a small diary where I write the names of new plants and note when I sowed their seeds. This diary helps me remember what worked and what did not.

My Hobby Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

My favourite hobby is gardening. I grow flowers, herbs, and a few vegetables in pots and in a small patch beside our home. I loosen the soil, sow seeds, water the plants, and remove weeds. Watching a seed become a living plant teaches me patience and care, because a plant does not grow in a single day. I have learned the names of many plants and flowers, and I enjoy seeing bees and butterflies visit my garden.

Gardening refreshes me after study and gives me gentle exercise. It takes my mind away from books and mobile screens for a while, and the fresh air makes me feel calm. Green plants make the surroundings cooler and more attractive, while herbs and vegetables can provide fresh food for my family. I reuse kitchen containers as planters, collect rainwater when I can, and avoid wasting water. Sometimes I share seedlings with my neighbours, and we exchange advice about plants. This hobby has made me more interested in nature and more aware that healthy surroundings depend on daily responsibility. A small garden can teach us that good results need regular work, not only big plans. On weekends, I sometimes visit a nursery to learn about new plants and to buy seeds for the next season. The nursery workers often give useful advice about soil, water, and sunlight, and I try to follow their suggestions at home. Gardening has also taught me the value of patience, because a garden rewards those who wait and work steadily.

My Hobby Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

My favourite hobby is gardening. I grow flowers, herbs, and a few vegetables in pots and in a small patch beside our home. I loosen the soil, sow seeds, water the plants, and remove weeds. Watching a seed become a living plant teaches me patience and care, because a plant does not grow in a single day. I have learned the names of many plants and flowers, and I enjoy seeing bees and butterflies visit my garden. When a plant I planted with my own hands begins to flower, I feel a quiet joy that no bought thing can give.

Gardening refreshes me after study and gives me gentle exercise. It takes my mind away from books and mobile screens for a while, and the fresh air makes me feel calm and cheerful. Green plants make the surroundings cooler and more attractive, while herbs and vegetables can provide fresh food for my family. A garden also helps the environment, because plants give oxygen and keep the air clean. I reuse kitchen containers as planters, collect rainwater when I can, and avoid wasting water. Sometimes I share seedlings with my neighbours, and we exchange advice about plants and seeds.

This hobby has made me more interested in nature and more aware that healthy surroundings depend on daily responsibility. It has taught me that good results need regular work, not only big plans. A hobby should give both pleasure and learning, and gardening gives me both. I hope to make my garden bigger one day and to teach my younger brother how to plant and care for trees. When friends visit my home, I show them my garden first, and many of them have started small gardens of their own. That is the best reward of a hobby.

Early Rising Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

Early rising means getting up from bed early in the morning. It is a very good habit. There is a famous saying, "Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise." An early riser can enjoy the fresh air of the morning and the beauty of nature. The morning is calm and quiet, so a student can study with full attention.

A person who rises early gets more time for his work. He can take exercise, say his prayers, and prepare his lessons before school. He can finish his work in time and never feels hurried. On the other hand, a late riser wakes up late, misses the fresh morning, and cannot finish his work properly. He becomes lazy and falls behind in life.

Early rising is good for health, mind, and study. So every student should try to form this good habit from an early age.

Early Rising Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

Early rising means getting up from bed early in the morning. It is one of the best habits a person can form. There is a famous saying, "Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise." This saying is true. The morning is the best part of the day. The air is fresh, nature is calm and beautiful.

An early riser gets many benefits. First, he can enjoy the fresh morning air and take exercise or go for a walk. This keeps his body healthy and his mind fresh. Second, the morning is quiet, so a student can study with full concentration. Lessons learned in the morning are remembered easily. Third, an early riser gets more time for his work. He can say his prayers, prepare his lessons, and plan his day without hurry. He can finish his work in time and reach school punctually.

On the other hand, a late riser loses all these benefits. He wakes up late, feels lazy, and cannot finish his work in time. He often misses his lessons and falls behind in his studies. He becomes dull and inactive.

However, early rising is useful only when a person also goes to bed early and gets enough sleep. A student who stays awake late at night and wakes up early will feel tired, not fresh. So we should form the habit of sleeping early and rising early. It is a simple habit, but it can make our life healthy, disciplined, and successful.

Early Rising Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

Early rising means the habit of getting up from bed early in the morning. It is one of the best habits in human life. There is a well-known saying, "Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise." This old saying is still true today, because the habit of rising early brings many benefits to our body, mind, and work.

The morning is the most beautiful and peaceful part of the day. At that time, nature looks fresh, the air is pure, and everything is calm and quiet. He can go for a walk or take exercise, which keeps his body strong and his mind fresh for the whole day.

Early rising is especially useful for students. The morning hours are quiet, and there is no noise to disturb the mind. So a student can study with full concentration and remember his lessons easily. He can revise his lessons, prepare his homework, and plan his day before going to school. Punctuality and discipline grow from this habit.

A late riser, on the other hand, loses all these advantages. He wakes up late, feels lazy, and rushes through his work. He often misses his lessons, reaches school late, and falls behind in his studies. His health also suffers because he misses the fresh air and exercise of the morning.

But early rising is helpful only when it is joined with early sleeping. A person who stays awake till late at night and then wakes up early will be tired and dull. So we should go to bed early, sleep well, and rise early. If we form this habit from our student life, we can enjoy a healthy, disciplined, and successful life. This habit also builds confidence and a strong character.

Deforestation Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

Deforestation means cutting down trees in large numbers and clearing forests. Trees are very useful to us. They give us oxygen, wood, fruits, and shade. They also give shelter to birds and animals. But people are cutting down trees for wood, fuel, furniture, and land for houses, roads, and farms.

Deforestation causes great harm to our environment. Trees also bring rain and keep the soil rich and fertile for farming. When trees are cut down, the amount of carbon dioxide in the air increases, and the earth becomes warmer. Rainfall becomes irregular, and the soil loses its fertility. Floods and droughts become more common. Many birds and animals lose their homes and die.

We must stop deforestation to save our earth. We should plant more trees and take care of them. If we cut down one tree, we should plant two trees. Let us all plant trees and protect our forests.

Deforestation Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

Deforestation means the cutting down of trees in large numbers and the clearing of forests. Forests are one of the greatest gifts of nature. Trees give us oxygen to breathe, absorb carbon dioxide from the air, and keep the earth cool. They give us wood, fruits, flowers, and medicine. They also give shelter to birds and animals and protect the soil from erosion. But people are destroying forests for their own needs.

There are many causes of deforestation. Our population is growing fast, so more land is needed for houses, roads, schools, and farms. Trees are cut down for timber, firewood, furniture, and paper. Some dishonest people cut down valuable trees illegally and sell them for money. In the hilly areas, forests are also cleared for shifting cultivation.

The effects of deforestation are very harmful. When trees are cut down, carbon dioxide increases in the air, and the world becomes warmer. Rainfall becomes irregular, and the fertile soil is washed away by rain. As a result, floods, droughts, and cyclones become more frequent. Many birds and animals lose their homes, and some species are in danger of extinction. In Bangladesh, the Sundarbans, our great mangrove forest, is also under threat.

To prevent deforestation, we must plant more trees and protect our forests. The government should enforce strict laws against illegal logging and start tree plantation programmes. Every student should plant at least one tree every year and take care of it.

Deforestation Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

Deforestation means the large-scale cutting down of trees and the clearing of forests. Forests are one of the most precious gifts of nature to mankind. Trees give us oxygen to breathe and absorb the harmful carbon dioxide from the air. They give us timber, fuel, fruits, flowers, and medicine. They bring rainfall, keep the soil fertile, and give shelter to countless birds, animals, and insects.

But people are destroying forests at an alarming rate. The main cause is the rapid growth of population. More people need more houses, roads, schools, and farmland, so forests are cleared to make room for them. Trees are cut down for timber, firewood, furniture, and paper. Some dishonest people cut down valuable trees illegally and sell the timber for quick money. In the hilly districts, forests are also cleared for shifting cultivation.

The effects of deforestation are very serious. When trees are cut down, carbon dioxide increases in the atmosphere, and the earth becomes warmer. Without the roots of trees to hold it, the fertile top soil is washed away by rain, and the land becomes barren. Floods, droughts, and cyclones become more frequent. Many species of birds and animals lose their homes, and some are in danger of extinction. In Bangladesh, the Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest in the world, protects our coast from cyclones, but it is also under threat from deforestation.

To save our environment, we must stop deforestation and plant more trees. The government should enforce strict laws against illegal logging, expand social forestry, and start a tree plantation movement in which every student plants at least one tree every year. We should also use wood carefully and raise public awareness about the value of forests. If we protect our forests today, we can leave a green and safe Bangladesh for the coming generations.

Bangla Meaning of Deforestation Paragraph

বন উজাড় অনুচ্ছেদের বাংলা অর্থ

বন উজাড় মানে প্রচুর সংখ্যায় গাছ কেটে ফেলা এবং বন ধ্বংস করা। গাছ আমাদের জন্য খুবই উপকারী। এগুলো আমাদের অক্সিজেন, কাঠ, ফল ও ছায়া দেয়। এগুলো পাখি ও পশুদের আশ্রয়ও দেয়। কিন্তু মানুষ কাঠ, জ্বালানি, আসবাবপত্র এবং বাড়ি, রাস্তা ও খামারের জমির জন্য গাছ কাটছে।

বন উজাড় আমাদের পরিবেশের বড় ক্ষতি করে। গাছ কাটা হলে বাতাসে কার্বন ডাই-অক্সাইডের পরিমাণ বেড়ে যায় এবং পৃথিবী আরও গরম হয়ে ওঠে। বৃষ্টিপাত অনিয়মিত হয় এবং মাটি তার উর্বরতা হারায়। বন্যা ও খরা আরও বেশি ঘটে। অনেক পাখি ও পশু তাদের বাসস্থান হারিয়ে মারা যায়।

পৃথিবীকে বাঁচাতে আমাদের বন উজাড় বন্ধ করতে হবে। আমাদের আরও বেশি গাছ লাগাতে হবে এবং সেগুলোর যত্ন নিতে হবে। একটি গাছ কাটলে আমাদের দুটি গাছ লাগানো উচিত। আসুন আমরা সবাই গাছ লাগাই এবং আমাদের বন রক্ষা করি।

Eve Teasing Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

"Eve-teasing" is a common term for unwanted comments, gestures, following, staring, or other harassment directed at girls and women. It is not harmless fun. It creates fear, restricts movement, interrupts education, and denies a person the right to travel safely.

Families and schools should teach respect, equality, consent, and responsible conduct from an early age. Witnesses can support the victim, seek help from trusted adults or authorities, and avoid blaming the person who was harassed. Communities need safe transport, lighting, complaint systems, and prompt enforcement of the law. Public spaces become safer when every person rejects harassment and protects the dignity of others. Boys and men must understand that silence and peer approval can encourage abuse, and that real respect means speaking up against it. A girl should never be told to change her education, clothing, or dreams to suit someone else's misconduct.

Eve Teasing Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

"Eve-teasing" is a common term for unwanted comments, gestures, following, staring, or other harassment directed at girls and women. It is not harmless fun. It creates fear, restricts movement, interrupts education, and denies a person the right to travel safely. A girl who faces harassment on the way to school may start missing classes, and some girls even drop out of school because of it. The harm is not only physical; it also damages confidence and peace of mind.

Families and schools should teach respect, equality, consent, and responsible conduct from an early age. Boys must learn that a girl's silence is not permission, and that no one has the right to comment on another person's body or clothes. Witnesses can support the victim, seek help from trusted adults or authorities, and avoid blaming the person who was harassed. A girl should never be told to change her education, clothing, or dreams to accommodate someone else's misconduct.

Communities need safe transport, good lighting, easy complaint systems, and prompt enforcement of the law. Schools and colleges should have clear rules against harassment and a safe way to report it. Public spaces become safer when every person rejects harassment and protects the dignity of others. Schools should also keep a trusted teacher or counsellor whom students can tell about harassment without fear of blame or punishment. When victims are heard and believed, other girls also find the courage to speak. That is how change begins.

Eve Teasing Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

"Eve-teasing" is a common term for unwanted comments, gestures, following, staring, or other harassment directed at girls and women. It is not harmless fun. It creates fear, restricts movement, interrupts education, and denies a person the right to travel safely. Girls should be taught that harassment is never their fault, and that they have the right to speak up. Witnesses can support the victim, seek help from trusted adults or authorities, and avoid blaming the person who was harassed. Silence and peer approval can encourage abuse, so friends must speak against it instead of laughing along.

Communities need safe transport, good lighting, easy complaint systems, and prompt enforcement of the law. Schools and colleges should have clear rules against harassment and a safe way to report it without fear. A girl should never be told to change her education, clothing, or dreams to accommodate someone else's misconduct. Public spaces become safer when every person rejects harassment and protects the dignity of others. Laws against harassment already exist, but they work only when complaints are taken seriously and punished quickly. The police, the courts, and the community must all do their part so that no harasser feels safe.

Physical Exercise Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

Physical exercise means moving the body in a planned and healthy way. Walking, running, swimming, cycling, gardening and playing games are all good forms of exercise. It makes our muscles strong, improves blood circulation, and helps us keep a healthy weight. It also keeps the mind fresh and cheerful.

A student who exercises regularly can study with better concentration. Exercise teaches discipline, patience and teamwork. Games teach us to follow rules and to accept both victory and defeat gracefully.

We should exercise every day, even if only for a short time. A morning walk or an evening game is enough for most students. We should warm up before exercise, drink enough water, and stop if we feel unwell. Good food and enough sleep are also necessary for good health.

In short, physical exercise keeps the body fit and the mind active. It is a habit that brings health, happiness and success in life.

Physical Exercise Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

Physical exercise means moving the body in a planned and healthy way. Walking, running, swimming, cycling, gardening and playing outdoor games are all good forms of exercise. It makes our muscles strong, improves blood circulation, and helps us keep a healthy weight. It also keeps the mind fresh, cheerful and ready to learn. A healthy body is the foundation of a happy and useful life.

A student who exercises regularly can study with better concentration. Exercise teaches discipline, patience and teamwork. In games we learn to follow rules, to cooperate with others, and to accept both victory and defeat gracefully. These lessons are as valuable in life as they are on the playground. Regular exercise also improves sleep and reduces stress, which helps students perform better in examinations.

We should exercise every day, even if only for a short time. A morning walk, a short run or an evening game is enough for most students. We should warm up before exercise, drink enough water, and stop if we feel unwell. People who are old or weak should begin with gentle walking and stretching. Good food and enough sleep are also necessary for good health. Many forms of exercise are free, so lack of money need not prevent a healthy routine.

In short, physical exercise keeps the body fit and the mind active. It protects us from many diseases and fills life with energy. We should avoid sitting for long hours and make movement part of everyday life. A person who exercises regularly can work, study and enjoy life much better.

Physical Exercise Paragraph in 300 Words

Physical exercise means moving the body in a planned and healthy way. Walking, running, swimming, cycling, gardening and playing outdoor games are all good forms of exercise. It makes our muscles strong, improves blood circulation, and helps us keep a healthy weight. It also keeps the mind fresh, cheerful and ready to learn. Good food and enough sleep are also necessary for good health. Many forms of exercise are free, so lack of money need not prevent a healthy routine.

In short, physical exercise keeps the body fit and the mind active. It protects us from many diseases, gives us energy for work and study, and fills life with joy. We should avoid sitting for long hours and make movement part of everyday life. A person who exercises regularly can work, study and enjoy life much better than one who lives a lazy life. So let us make exercise a daily habit from today.

On this page you will find a Gender Discrimination paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end.

Gender Discrimination Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

Gender discrimination means treating people differently because they are male or female. It can appear at home, in school, at work, or in public life. For example, a girl may be discouraged from studying, while a boy may be excused from household duties. Such attitudes prevent families and nations from using the abilities of all their citizens.

Everyone deserves equal respect, education, safety, and a fair chance to work. Parents should give sons and daughters the same encouragement, and schools should challenge unfair stereotypes. Laws can protect equal rights, but lasting change also depends on everyday behaviour. When women and men share responsibilities and opportunities, families become stronger and society makes better progress. Teachers should also give girls and boys equal chances in class, in sports, and in leadership roles at school. Equal treatment in small things builds equal respect in big things.

Gender Discrimination Paragraph in 250 Words

Best for Class 8–10 and SSC.

Gender discrimination means treating people differently because they are male or female. It can appear at home, in school, at work, or in public life. For example, a girl may be discouraged from studying, while a boy may be excused from household duties. A woman may be paid less for the same work, or a man may be laughed at for choosing a job that people call a woman's job. Such attitudes prevent families and nations from using the abilities of all their citizens.

Everyone deserves equal respect, education, safety, and a fair chance to work. A girl has the same right as a boy to go to school, to choose a subject she likes, and to dream of a career. Parents should give sons and daughters the same encouragement, and teachers should praise ability, not gender. Schools should challenge unfair stereotypes in books, stories, and everyday talk.

Laws can protect equal rights, but lasting change also depends on everyday behaviour. Boys should learn to share household work, and girls should be given confidence to speak and lead. When women and men share responsibilities and opportunities, families become stronger and society makes better progress. A country cannot move forward if half of its people are held back. In many families, parents still spend more on a son's education than on a daughter's, and this unfair habit must change if society wants real progress. Both sons and daughters can bring honour to a family.

Gender Discrimination Paragraph in 300 Words

Best for SSC and HSC.

Gender discrimination means treating people differently because they are male or female. It can appear at home, in school, at work, or in public life. For example, a girl may be discouraged from studying, while a boy may be excused from household duties. A woman may be paid less for the same work, or a man may be laughed at for choosing a job that people call a woman's job. Girls may be married early instead of finishing their education, and boys may be told that cooking or caring for children is not their work. Such attitudes prevent families and nations from using the abilities of all their citizens.

Everyone deserves equal respect, education, safety, and a fair chance to work. A girl has the same right as a boy to go to school, to choose a subject she likes, and to dream of a career. Parents should give sons and daughters the same encouragement, and teachers should praise ability, not gender. Schools should challenge unfair stereotypes in books, stories, and everyday talk, and they should give girls and boys the same chances in sports, leadership, and science.

Laws can protect equal rights, but lasting change also depends on everyday behaviour. Boys should learn to share household work, and girls should be given confidence to speak and lead. Workplaces should judge people by their skills and hard work, not by their gender. When women and men share responsibilities and opportunities, families become stronger and society makes better progress. A country cannot move forward if half of its people are held back, because talent is not limited to one gender. The media also has a role to play, because films, advertisements, and stories that show women as weak or men as careless only strengthen old stereotypes. Fair stories build a fair society.

Facebook Paragraph in 150 Words

Best for Class 6–7.

Facebook is a social networking service that connects people across the world. Users can create a profile, add friends, share photographs and videos, join groups, follow news pages, and send messages. It helps relatives and friends who live far apart stay in touch, and it helps students learn new things through educational pages and groups. Small businesses also use Facebook to show their products and reach customers.

However, Facebook has some dangers. False news spreads quickly, and strangers can misuse personal information. Spending too much time scrolling can waste study time and disturb sleep. Users should keep their privacy settings strong, accept friend requests carefully, and never share passwords or personal details with strangers. They should check a news item before sharing it and use polite language in comments. Facebook is useful when it is used for learning and communication, but it becomes harmful when it replaces study, sleep, and real friendship.

Facebook Paragraph in 250 Words

Facebook is a social networking service that connects people across the world. A user can create a profile, add friends, share photographs and videos, join groups, follow news pages, and send messages.
